questions.question: Plasma is often called the ______ state of matter.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**fourth.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Plasma** is often called the **fourth state of matter** because it has **unique properties** that distinguish it from the other** three states** (solid, liquid, and gas).
 
• Plasma is a state of matter in which a** gas is ionized, **meaning that some or all of its** atoms** have **lost or gained electrons.**
 
• This creates a mixture of** positively charged ions** and** negatively charged electrons **that can conduct** electricity **and respond to** magnetic fields.**
 
• Plasma is found in many natural and artificial environments, including **lightning, stars, flames, **and some types of** lamps.**
 
• It can also be** created in laboratories** by heating or applying **electric fields to gases.**
 
• Plasma has several practical applications, such as in **plasma cutting and welding, plasma TVs and displays**, and **plasma thrusters** for **spacecraft.**
 
• The idea of plasma as a distinct state of matter was first proposed by the** American physicist Irving Langmuir **in the **1920s,** based on his studies of **electric discharges in gases.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__

 
• Ninth and eighth are **not correct** because there are only **four known states of matter,** not nine or eight.

 
 
• However, some scientists have proposed **additional states or sub-states of matter** based on different criteria, such as **quark-gluon plasma or Bose-Einstein condensates.**
 
 
 
• **Sixth** is also **incorrect** because there are only four states of matter, not six.

questions.question: Which of the following is considered to be the fifth state of matter?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is ​__Bose-Einstein condensate.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Matters are generally categorized into 3 states:

 
 
• Solid: Particles are held very close to each other and can't move. 
 
• Liquid: Particles are close to each other but they can move around. 
 
• Gas: Particles are far from each other as compared to those present in solid or liquid states and their movement is easy and fast. 
 
 
 
• Two more states are discovered under extreme circumstances:
 
 
• Plasma: A superheated matter, so hot that the electrons are ripped away from the atoms forming an ionized gas. 
 
• Bose-Einstein Condensate: A group of atoms cooled to absolute zero temperature(-273.15 °C). 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a011bf8a910ec1efc0e385b00fd7aa98c90ad04710d9dd6a3c46f121360ce89c.png]

questions.question: Which of the following state of matter is also known as Bose-Einstein condensate?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fifth.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

__
 
• Bose-Einstein Condensate is called the Fifth state of matter.
 
• It is formed when a gas of bosons having low densities is cooled to absolute zero temperature.
 
• At this temperature, the atoms stop moving.
 
• They thus clump to each other acting like a single atom with the whole group having identical physical properties.
 
• Plasma is a subset of gas which unlike the ordinary gases, is made up of atoms where some or all the electrons are stripped and positively charged protons roam freely.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• States of Matter: There are five states of matter.
 
 
• Solid
 
• Liquid
 
• Gas
 
• Plasma
 
• Bose-Eienstein Condensate(BEC)

questions.question: Select the INCORRECT statement from the following.

options.text: Both boiling and evaporation are bulk phenomena.

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Both boiling and evaporation are bulk phenomena.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Boiling** is a bulk phenomenon as it involves the entire liquid reaching the boiling point and turning into vapor.
 
• **Evaporation** is a surface phenomenon that occurs at the surface of the liquid, where molecules escape into the air at temperatures below the boiling point.
 
• Since **evaporation** only affects the surface and not the entire liquid, it is not considered a bulk phenomenon.
 
• **Evaporation** causes cooling because the molecules with higher energy escape, leaving the remaining molecules with lower average energy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Boiling**__

 __
 
• **Boiling** occurs when the liquid's temperature reaches its boiling point, causing vaporization throughout the liquid.
 
• This involves the formation of bubbles within the liquid that rise to the surface and burst.
 
• It is a rapid process compared to **evaporation**.
 
 
 
• **Evaporation**__
 
 
• **Evaporation** occurs at any temperature, as long as the liquid's molecules have enough energy to escape into the gas phase.
 
• This process is usually slower and happens over a larger period.
 
• Examples of **evaporation** include the drying of clothes and the cooling effect of sweat on the skin.

questions.question: At 10 × 10⁴ Pa pressure and 300 K temperature, the volume of 0.09 mol CO₂ gas is 22.4 × 10−³ m³. What will be the volume of the gas if the pressure is decreased to 2 × 10⁴ Pa?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**112.0 × 10⁻³ m³**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• To calculate the **volume of a gas** under different pressure conditions, we use **Boyle's Law**.
 
• **Boyle's Law** states that, at constant temperature, the pressure of a gas is inversely proportional to its volume. Mathematically, it is expressed as:

 **P₁V₁ = P₂V₂**, where:
 
 
• **P₁** and **V₁** are the initial pressure and volume.
 
• **P₂** and **V₂** are the final pressure and volume.
 
 
 
• In this case:
 
 
• Initial pressure (**P₁**) = **10 × 10⁴ Pa**.
 
• Initial volume (**V₁**) = **22.4 × 10⁻³ m³**.
 
• Final pressure (**P₂**) = **2 × 10⁴ Pa**.
 
 
 
• Rearranging Boyle's Law to solve for **V₂**:

 **V₂ = (P₁ × V₁) / P₂**.
 
• Substituting the values:

 **V₂ = (10 × 10⁴ × 22.4 × 10⁻³) / (2 × 10⁴)**.

 **V₂ = 112.0 × 10⁻³ m³**.
 
• Hence, the final volume of the gas when the pressure is reduced to **2 × 10⁴ Pa** is **112.0 × 10⁻³ m³**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Key Concepts of Boyle's Law:**

 
 
• Boyle's Law is valid only if the **temperature** and the **amount of gas (number of moles)** remain constant.
 
• The law is widely used in understanding and calculating gas behaviors in **closed systems**.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Boyle's Law:**
 
 
• Boyle's Law is applied in fields such as **pneumatics, scuba diving, and the design of syringes**.
 
• It is also used in the study of **breathing mechanisms** in humans and animals.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a noble gas?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Oxygen**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Oxygen** is a colourless, odourless, and tasteless gas that is taken up by animals, which then convert it to carbon dioxide; plants, on the other hand, use carbon dioxide as a carbon source and return oxygen to the environment.
 
• Oxygen produces compounds when it reacts with nearly every other element, as well as when it reacts with other elements to displace them from their combinations; in many circumstances, these reactions are accompanied by the evolution of heat and light and are referred to as combustions.
 
• Water is the most crucial component.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Neon** is a chemical element with the atomic number 10 and the symbol Ne. It's classified as a noble gas.
 
• **Krypton **is an **atomic number 36** chemical element with the **symbol Kr.**
 
• **Argon **is a chemical element in the periodic table's eighteen groups. It is an **atomic number 18** and the **symbol Ar.** 
 
 
• It is the third most abundant gas in the earth's atmosphere and is a noble gas.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b22825115bb18b37faedf6a4557e1773697b1dc5f616aa1aaa4f7f9aced0cc8d.png]

questions.question: The liquid water present in oceans, lakes and rivers gets converted to the gaseous form in the presence of sunlight in the water cycle. This step is called:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Evaporation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Evaporation is the process by which water changes from a liquid to a gas or vapor.
 
• In the water cycle, evaporation is driven by the heat energy from the sun.
 
• This process primarily occurs at the surface of bodies of water like oceans, lakes, and rivers.
 
• Evaporation is a crucial step in the water cycle, contributing to the formation of clouds and precipitation.
 
• It helps in regulating temperature and is essential for maintaining the earth's climate.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Condensation**

 
 
• Condensation is the process where water vapor becomes liquid.
 
• It occurs when the air is saturated with water vapor and cools down.
 
• This process is responsible for the formation of clouds and dew.
 
 
 
• **Precipitation**
 
 
• Precipitation includes various forms of water, such as rain, sleet, snow, and hail, that fall from the sky.
 
• It is a key component of the water cycle, returning water to the Earth's surface.
 
 
 
• **Melting**
 
 
• Melting is the process by which a solid turns into a liquid due to heat.
 
• In the context of the water cycle, it refers to the melting of ice and snow into liquid water.
 
 
 
• **The Water Cycle**
 
 
• The water cycle is a continuous process by which water circulates throughout the Earth and its atmosphere.
 
• It includes processes like evaporation, condensation, precipitation, infiltration, and runoff.
 
• This cycle is vital for sustaining life on Earth.

questions.question: Which of the following two properties of metals are exploited to prepare very thin sheets of silver to decorate sweets?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Malleability and Lustre**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Malleability** is the property of metals that allows them to be hammered or rolled into thin sheets without breaking. This property is crucial in preparing thin sheets of silver for decorative purposes.
 
• **Lustre** refers to the shiny appearance of metals due to their ability to reflect light. This makes silver sheets visually appealing when used for decorating sweets.
 
• Silver, being a highly malleable metal, can be easily converted into sheets as thin as a few microns without losing its structural integrity.
 
• The combination of malleability and lustre makes silver ideal for use in food decoration, particularly in Indian sweets like barfis and laddoos, where the thin silver sheets are known as **“varak” or “vark”**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Malleability**

 
 
• Malleability is a physical property of materials, specifically metals, that allows them to withstand deformation under compressive stress.
 
• Other highly malleable metals include gold, aluminum, and copper.
 
• This property is utilized in various industries, including jewelry making, coin minting, and decorative applications.
 
 
 
• **Lustre**
 
 
• Lustre is the optical property of metals that gives them their characteristic shine or reflective surface.
 
• Metals like silver, gold, and platinum are known for their high lustre and are often used in decorative and ornamental applications.
 
 
 
• **Silver Varak (Edible Silver Foil)**
 
 
• Varak is an ultra-thin sheet of pure silver used to decorate sweets, desserts, and sometimes even savory dishes in Indian cuisine.
 
• It is made by placing small silver pieces between layers of parchment and hammering them until they form extremely thin sheets.
 
• The silver foil is safe for consumption as it is biologically inert and passes through the digestive system without causing harm.
 
 
 
• **Other Properties of Silver**
 
 
• Silver is an excellent conductor of heat and electricity, making it valuable in industrial applications.
 
• It is highly ductile, allowing it to be stretched into thin wires, but ductility is not utilized for making sheets.
